text: Tools forged from Manifested Ingots: a pickaxe, axe, shovel, blade, shears and hoe. They cut like diamond and each lasts **1,024** uses.
While they can draw Pulse from a carried cell they spare their edge: every paid block or use mends a point of wear instead of costing one, and a paid blow costs none.

The [Pulse Bow](song_bench) and [Pulse Crossbow](pulse_crossbow) are forged from Manifested Ingots too and last as long, but every shot wears them a point. All of it mends at the [Spirit Anvil](spirit_anvil).
pages.title: Spiritgear tools
Pulse for work
text: A block mined costs **2 Pulse**, a hit **3**, a use **1**, taken from any Pulse Cell you carry.
With no Pulse the tool still works, but it wears like any other tool, and the action bar tells you it is starving.
An attuned [familiar](familiar_boons) of a piece's voice nearby cuts what it spends by **40%**. The pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe and blade also mend with diamonds on any anvil.

pages.title: Ranking up
text: Ranks are where Spiritgear becomes something special, and they are meant to take real effort. Seat the piece in the station with its totem nearby, put the **catalysts** in the catalyst slots, and keep the Pulse flowing:
- **Echo Attune**, Fire: rank 0 to 1. **45 seconds** at **96 Pulse a second**, and **4 Attuned Echo**.
- **Echo Bind**, Water: rank 1 to 2. **90 seconds** at **128**, and **4 Bound Echo**.
- **Echo Manifest**, Spirit: rank 2 to 3. **180 seconds** at **192**, and **2 Resonant Cores** and **4 Loom Thread**.

pages.title: Before you rank
text: Each station takes only the next rank: Bind refuses rank 0, and Manifest refuses anything below Bound. Loom Thread only comes from [The Unsung](the_unsung), so the top rank waits until you have beaten it.
Those are heavy draws for any camp. Bring a Resonator with a good catalyst, or several generators, within 8 blocks.
The station waits, spending nothing, until its catalysts are in; they are used up when the rank lands. The tooltip always shows what the next rank needs.

pages.title: What ranks give
text: - **Attuned**: every action costs one Pulse less, never below one (mining 1, a hit 2, a use 1), mines **20%** faster, and hits harder.
- **Bound**: a starved swing does not wear the tool, and it mines **45%** faster.
- **Manifested**: mines **80%** faster, half of starved swings even mend a point, and voice perks grow stronger.

The blade and its [weapon family](spiritgear_weapons) gain the most: **+2**, **+5** and **+10** attack damage by rank, and a little attack speed. A Manifested blade hits **bosses 25% harder** and heals you for **10%** of every blow, which is what you want in a long fight.
A Loom-linked pick spends **0 Pulse** to mine. Echo Unweave takes a damaged tool back apart into one Manifested Ingot, forgetting rank and voice.

pages.title: The shears
text: The **Spiritgear Shears** trim leaves, wool, vines and cobweb, and rank and take a voice like the rest of the set.
- **Earth**: a swing takes the whole 3x3 face of foliage.
- **Air**: trimming costs no Pulse and no wear at all.
- **Water**: a sheared sheep keeps its fleece half the time, and always at Manifested.
- **Fire**: used on a beehive it smokes the bees calm, so no swarm.
- **Spirit**: what it shears is mended afterwards, and nearby beasts worth shearing glow.
- **Loom**: the cuttings come straight to hand.

pages.title: The hoe
text: The **Spiritgear Hoe** reaps and sows in one motion: use it on a ripe crop and the harvest drops, less one seed that goes straight back into the ground. A crop that gives no seed of its own is reaped and left bare.
- **Earth**: turns a 3x3 of soil at once.
- **Water**: its furrows come out wet, and farmland around you stays watered while you hold it.
- **Air**: reaps a 3x3.
- **Loom**: reaps a 5x5 and spends no Pulse doing it.
- **Spirit**: a quarter of harvests drop double (seeds aside).

pages.title: A cell of its own
text: Every piece of Spiritgear and Spiritweave, the [Resonance Maul](resonance_maul), the [Sixfold Staff](sixfold_staff), songbooks and the Pulse bows can carry a **Pulse Cell** of its own. Pick the cell up in your inventory and **right-click it onto the piece**: it goes inside, charge and all.
The piece always spends from its own cell first. Only when that cell is empty does it reach for the cells you carry, so a well-charged set keeps going long after your pockets run dry.

pages.title: Swapping cells
text: Right-click a bigger cell (a **{item:tribalpower:greater_pulse_cell}** or a **{item:tribalpower:grand_pulse_cell}**) onto a piece holding a smaller one to upgrade it; the old cell comes back to your cursor. A cell of the same size or smaller tops the seated one up instead.
Right-click a piece with an **empty cursor** to take its cell back out, charge and all. The tooltip shows what each piece holds.
